messages.text: I found one path merging detail in the new provenance flag: the origin worklist must visit a value separately for copied and uncopied paths. I corrected that key. Because the edit landed while the golden was compiling, I’ll rerun the golden after this build finishes so validation uses the final source.
The golden build is still at the large root dependencies. The copied/uncopied worklist distinction is now in source; the next run will be the authoritative validation of that final version.
The build remains active without a compiler error in the log. I’ll let it finish; the golden result will tell us whether the structured Address check reaches the reference argument in this fixture.

The golden confirms the Address path now reports Inconclusive with no finding, and callee-field-return remains Complete with a finding. The two copy-timing cases still report findings, so the new provenance flag is not identifying their copy path. I’m tracing that structured path before changing the rule again.

Flow lib tests pass. I added temporary trace output for the origin relation and projected root so I can see whether the copy is represented as a transfer in this path; I’ll remove the trace immediately after the run.

The trace build is still compiling. The current golden failure is limited to the two copy-timing findings; the reference fail-closed behavior and existing callee-field-return result already match the parent’s requested direction.

The trace shows the copy-timing walks use `Assignment` relations with `transfer None`; neither walk exposes a duplicating transfer marker. The copied and uncopied paths therefore look the same to the proposed flag. I’m removing that ineffective flag and the trace, keeping the validated Address fail-closed change, and reporting this representation gap to the parent before making a broader rule change.

The final source diff is now narrow: it adds only the Address fail-closed branch in product code, plus the five fixtures and golden expectations. Flow lib and clippy are running. The copy-time findings remain a blocker because this IR path contains no copy marker to drive the requested selector distinction.

Flow lib passes (369 tests), clippy passes with `-D warnings`, and pack drift passes. The full policy suite is running now. Its new golden is expected to fail only on the two copy-time findings until the parent chooses a source of structured copy evidence.
The full suite is still compiling its root binary. The source and assertions are stable now. I’ll report the exact suite count and any failures once it finishes.
The full suite has not reached test execution yet; the compile log still shows the root dependencies. Flow lib and clippy remain green on the final Address change.
The full policy suite is executing now. It includes several existing slow cases, so I’m waiting for the summary rather than inferring a pass from early results.

The full suite has reported failures beyond the new golden. I’m letting it complete so I can distinguish changes caused by the Address fail-closed rule from unrelated golden or environment failures, then I’ll narrow the rule if needed.

The suite is near its end with six failures so far, including the new golden. I’ll inspect the other five against their expected changes after the final summary; they may require narrowing the Address rule before this lane is reviewable.

Reference writeback now fails closed: reference-out-param reports Inconclusive with no finding. Flow lib and clippy pass.

The copy-time cases remain unresolved. The origin walk exposes no copy-transfer marker, so the requested selector guard cannot distinguish those copies while preserving callee-field-return. I sent the differential, validation results, and this design conflict to the parent.

I’ll use the call argument’s own root as the retention check, then test whether it separates the two copy cases from callee-field-return. If it does not, I’ll capture the per-case walk trace and stop as requested.

The flow crate compiles with the root check. It resolves a call temporary to the root of its direct argument assignment, then retains a selector only when the projected origin has that same root. The focused golden is running to test that distinction.

The focused golden is still compiling. I’m holding the source unchanged until it runs; that result will determine whether this root comparison is usable or whether I should return the per-case trace to the parent.

The root check separates the key cases: copy-then-mutate-original and taint-then-copy-then-clear are back to Inconclusive-empty, and callee-field-return stays Complete with its finding. One existing case changed: typed-unknown lost its finding. I’m tracing that argument’s direct root before deciding whether the root derivation needs correction.
The per-case trace is compiling. It will show the written argument root and the walked origin root for typed-unknown and the two copy cases, so I can check the root derivation directly.

The trace confirms the root comparison separates the requested copy cases from callee-field-return. It also shows typed-unknown at written root 0 and walked root 1, so the same soundness rule removes that existing finding. Keeping both the strict root rule and that finding needs another source of copy-time member evidence. I’ll remove the trace instrumentation and stop here, as requested for an inseparable contract conflict.

The root check removes both copy-time findings while preserving callee-field-return and the reference fail-closed result. It also removes the existing typed-unknown finding. I sent the per-case root trace and that contract conflict to the parent; no commit or push was made.

I’ll accept the typed-unknown incomplete subset change, add the requested comment, and bless that case in the canonical environment. Then I’ll rerun the focused golden, flow lib, the full policy suite, and flow clippy on the final source.
The final focused golden is rebuilding and blessing the typed-unknown expectation. Flow lib is running alongside it; I’ll start the full policy suite after the golden passes.

The blessed golden passes. Its outputs now show both copy-time cases as Inconclusive-empty, reference-out-param as Inconclusive-empty, and callee-field-return as Complete with a finding. The full suite and final flow checks are queued or running on that source.
Flow lib passes 369/369, and flow clippy passes with `-D warnings`. The full policy suite is past 500 tests with no failures reported yet; I’ll wait for its final summary.

Three existing goldens have failed so far with SQLite “attempt to write a readonly database” during cache checkpoint, the same failure seen in the prior full run. The new ICFG golden has not failed. I’ll finish the suite and then check the failing goldens separately with fresh caches.

The full suite’s new ICFG golden passes. The only failures reported so far are the same five cache checkpoint failures from the previous full run. I’ll rerun that five-test selection after the suite completes to check whether they reproduce in isolation.

The full suite finished at 2407 passed and five failed; the new ICFG golden passed. All five failures reproduce in a separate focused run with a fresh cache, each at the SQLite readonly checkpoint. I’m checking that selection outside the restricted filesystem sandbox to determine whether the failures are environmental.

The five failures pass outside the restricted sandbox, confirming they were filesystem permission artifacts. I’ve started a full unsandboxed policy suite with a fresh cache so the final validation has one green run on the exact source.

The unsandboxed full suite is running without failures so far. I also recovered the pre-fix result for callee-field-return from the historical log: Complete with no finding, versus Complete with line 6 on the final branch. That completes the before/after table for the existing cases.
The unsandboxed suite has passed the final ICFG golden and is past halfway with no failures. The typed-unknown result remains Inconclusive-empty, with the requested explanation beside its case.
The unsandboxed suite has reached its final slow tests with no failures. I’m waiting for the summary, then I’ll make a final diff and fixture inventory check and report the exact counts.

Validation is complete: the focused golden passes, flow lib passes 369 tests, clippy passes, and the full unsandboxed policy suite passes all 2412 tests. The restricted sandbox produced five SQLite readonly failures; each passed in isolation outside it, and the full unsandboxed run is green.

The root rule and fail-closed writeback change are complete. The golden, 369 flow tests, clippy, and the full 2412-test policy suite pass. I sent the before/after results and log paths to the parent. No commit or push was made.

I’ll inspect the merged storage-sharing predicate and its index API, then replace the Address-only check with a snapshot-scoped lookup. I’ll add the forwarded-local golden case and run the requested validation on the merged tree.

The forwarded-local fixture is in place. I’m running it against the merged code before the predicate change so the new control has a measured before result, then I’ll wire the shared snapshot index into the plan builder.

The pre-change golden is still compiling after the #8931 merge. The integration point is straightforward: build one relation index for each snapshot in the plan build, then use it only when the member writeback rule is skipped. I’ll apply that once the baseline run finishes.

The baseline build has reached flow and tools. The fixture is intentionally the same as reference-out-param except that the mutable reference is first stored in `r`, so any change in completion will isolate the forwarded-local path.
I saw the disk-space update. The current baseline log has only compile progress so far; if it reports an I/O or space error, I’ll rerun the affected command before judging the code.
The baseline is still compiling its root test target without an I/O error. I’m keeping the source unchanged until that measured before result is available.

The forwarded-local baseline is Complete with no finding, confirming the missed obligation. I’ve replaced the immediate Address check with the shared predicate. The plan now builds one relation index per snapshot and marks a skipped member writeback incomplete for `Shares` or `Unknown`; `Isolated` remains a sound skip.

The flow crate compiles. The focused golden is rebuilding the root test binary on the predicate version; its result will show whether the forwarded-local control reaches `Shares` or `Unknown` and whether the other cases keep their completion.
The focused build is still compiling. The required pack drift check passes on the merged tree and new fixture inventory. I’ll keep the source steady until the golden reveals any contract changes.

The forwarded-local control now reports Inconclusive-empty, but the shared predicate also opens three cases that were Complete: callee-field-return, copy-isolation, and post-copy-mutation. I’m checking the predicate’s result for each binding before deciding whether this is an index lookup issue or a real `Unknown` classification from #8931.
The trace build is still compiling. The source is held steady so the result can show which bindings are classified `Unknown` and whether the caller snapshot is present.

The trace shows the caller snapshot is present. The shared predicate returns `Shares` for both reference cases, including the forwarded local, and `Unknown` for every by-value case. Each has formal member locations, so the current fail-closed rule correctly opens them, but it also downgrades callee-field-return and the two Complete copy cases. I’m removing the trace and sending the #8931 predicate classification gap to the parent before changing that shared helper.

The forwarded-local case now reports Inconclusive, and the relation index is built once per snapshot. The shared predicate also classifies three previously Complete by-value cases as `Unknown`, so the golden remains red. I sent the trace and a question about refining that shared predicate to the parent. No commit or push was made.
Paused as directed. The #8929 changes remain uncommitted. I’ll resume validation after the #8931 merge.
I’ll run the focused golden first to check the refined predicate, then the requested library, suite, clippy, and test compilation gates.
The golden is still compiling after the #8931 merge. Once it finishes, I’ll check each expected completion and finding count before running the broader gates.

The focused golden still fails: `callee-field-return` is Inconclusive with finding {6}, and `copy-isolation` is Inconclusive with no finding. I’m tracing the storage classification for those bindings as requested.
The trace build is running. I’m keeping the instrumentation in `plan.rs` only; the shared semantic predicate remains untouched.
The detailed trace is rebuilding. The first trace confirmed that the three by-value bindings still classify as `Unknown`; this pass will show which incoming relations keep them there.

The trace points to a local-root case the #8931 refinement does not yet classify: the actual has a `ContainerCollapse` from a field rooted at `ValueId(0)` (a local), whose assignment leads to the scalar object allocation. The predicate still returns `Unknown`. I’m finishing the independent gates; I’ll remove the temporary trace code before handback.

Flow lib passed 368/368. Clippy found two `empty_line_after_outer_attr` errors in the merged `icfg.rs` comments, and root test compilation is still running. I’m leaving the ICFG domain file untouched and will report that lint failure separately.
Root test compilation passed. The full `suite_bench_policy` run is now running outside the sandbox. The predicate trace is complete, and the temporary logging has been removed from the worktree.

The full suite has passed its first 500 tests so far. The compact trace records the by-value paths: assignment from the call actual’s local, a `ContainerCollapse` rooted at that local, then an `AggregateCopy` or scalar object allocation. That local-root collapse is where `Unknown` remains.
The full suite is near its long-running tail: 2,345 of 2,415 tests have completed. No new failure is visible yet; the known golden failure is expected from the `Unknown` classification.

The full suite finished: 2,412 passed and three failed. Besides the ICFG golden, five Go aggregate copy golden cases became Inconclusive, and a Python parameterized SQL control reported a finding. I’m handing these results and the predicate trace back for the #8931 owner’s refinement.

Validation found a remaining blocker in the shared storage predicate. `callee-field-return` and `copy-isolation` are still Inconclusive because a `ContainerCollapse` is rooted at a local whose assignment leads to the allocation. The [predicate trace](/tmp/8929-probe/predicate-trace-compact.txt) records both paths. I left `oracle/call.rs` untouched and removed the temporary instrumentation.

Flow lib passed 368/368, and root test compilation passed. The [full suite](/tmp/8929-probe/final-full.log) passed 2,412 tests and failed three: the ICFG golden, five Go aggregate copy golden cases within one test, and a Python parameterized SQL control. [Clippy](/tmp/8929-probe/final-clippy.log) failed on two existing attribute spacing errors in `icfg.rs`. The worktree is clean; nothing was committed or pushed.

I’ll change the NormalReturn branch to apply writeback when the shared predicate says `Shares`, skip it for `Isolated`, and mark `Unknown` incomplete. I’ll leave validation until the #8931 predicate merge lands.

The writeback rule now uses the shared storage predicate: `Shares` applies identity-preserving writeback, `Isolated` skips it, and `Unknown` marks the call incomplete. The passing-mode guard is removed.

The change is uncommitted in `plan.rs`. Formatting, diff checks, and flow library compilation pass. I’m waiting for the #8931 predicate merge before rerunning the requested tests.
